prompt:
You are checking which candidate answer correctly answers a question about a SQL database.

Question:
Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within any other packaging, have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500, and what are the names of both these containers and the corresponding items?

4 candidates were produced independently. Each shows its SQL and the first rows of its result.

[A]
SQL:
WITH RECURSIVE packaging_tree AS (
    SELECT 
        p.id AS container_id,
        p.id AS current_id,
        1 AS level,
        1.0::DOUBLE AS multiplier
    FROM packaging p
    WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        pt.container_id,
        pr.contains_id AS current_id,
        pt.level + 1,
        pt.multiplier * pr.qty::DOUBLE
    FROM packaging_tree pt
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = pt.current_id
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    p_container.name AS container_name,
    p_item.name AS item_name,
    SUM(pt.multiplier) AS total_qty
FROM packaging_tree pt
JOIN packaging p_container ON p_container.id = pt.container_id
JOIN packaging p_item ON p_item.id = pt.current_id
WHERE pt.level > 1
GROUP BY pt.container_id, p_container.name, p_item.name
HAVING SUM(pt.multiplier) > 500
ORDER BY p_container.name, p_item.name;

SQL:
WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy AS (
    -- Start with top-level containers (not contained in anything)
    SELECT p.id as root_id, p.id as current_id, 0 as level, CAST(1.0 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) as qty_multiplier
    FROM packaging p
    LEFT JOIN packaging_relations pr ON p.id = pr.contains_id
    WHERE pr.packaging_id IS NULL
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Get children and calculate multiplier
    SELECT h.root_id, pr.contains_id as current_id, h.level + 1, h.qty_multiplier * pr.qty
    FROM hierarchy h
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON h.current_id = pr.packaging_id
),
item_totals AS (
    -- Sum qty_multiplier for each item within each top-level container
    SELECT root_id, current_id as item_id, SUM(qty_multiplier) as total_qty
    FROM hierarchy
    GROUP BY root_id, current_id
)
SELECT 
    p_root.name as container_name,
    p_item.name as item_name
FROM item_totals it
JOIN packaging p_root ON it.root_id = p_root.id
JOIN packaging p_item ON it.item_id = p_item.id
WHERE it.total_qty > 500
ORDER BY container_name, item_name

WITH RECURSIVE top_level AS (
    SELECT id as container_id
    FROM packaging
    WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)
),
hierarchy AS (
    SELECT 
        tl.container_id as container_id,
        p.id as level_id,
        1 as multiplier
    FROM top_level tl
    JOIN packaging p ON tl.container_id = p.id
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        h.container_id,
        pr.contains_id as level_id,
        h.multiplier * pr.qty
    FROM hierarchy h
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON h.level_id = pr.packaging_id
),
-- Get products at each level
products_at_level AS (
    SELECT 
        h.container_id,
        h.level_id,
        p.id as product_id,
        h.multiplier as level_multiplier
    FROM hierarchy h
    JOIN packaging_relations rel ON h.level_id = rel.packaging_id
    JOIN packaging p ON rel.contains_id = p.id
),
-- Sum quantities per container and product
product_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        pal.container_id,
        pal.product_id,
        SUM(pal.level_multiplier) as total_qty
    FROM products_at_level pal
    GROUP BY pal.container_id, pal.product_id
)
SELECT 
    pt.container_id,
    p.name as container_name,
    pt.product_id,
    prod.name as product_name,
    pt.total_qty
FROM product_totals pt
JOIN packaging p ON pt.container_id = p.id
JOIN products prod ON pt.product_id = prod.id
